content.text:
I opened the dependency PR, [saranatour1/site#85](https://github.com/saranatour1/site/pull/85). Your three article changes are done and checked in the preview and a production build, on a separate `article-polish` branch from `main`. Nothing on that branch is committed yet.

**Title moving up**
- Clicking an article in the list now changes the address without a full page reload, and the title and description glide up and grow into their place on the article page.
- Going back reverses the animation.
- It uses Astro's built-in page transitions, which the site already had switched on, so no extra JavaScript ships.

**Smaller description:** the line under the title is now 18px (16px on phones), down from 22px.

**Photo**
- It's centered in the column, with a grey centered caption under it: "Me at 4 or 5, at my dad's PC, writing some Excel". That's my wording, so change it to whatever you like.
- The caption is written in the article itself with a `<figure>` wrapper. I've added the pattern to [docs/publishing-articles.md](docs/publishing-articles.md) so you can reuse it.

I first tried a Markdown plugin to add captions automatically, but Astro 7's default Markdown engine needs an extra package for plugins. Plain HTML in the article does the same job without it.

Animate article titles into place, center captioned photos

- Clicking an article in the list animates its title and description up
  into the article page (matching transition:name on both pages).
- The article description is smaller: 18px, 16px on phones.
- Article images are centered; a <figure> with <figcaption> gives them a
  centered caption. The first article's photo uses it, and the publishing
  guide shows the pattern.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git push -q -u origin article-polish 2>&1 | grep -v "^remote:\|entire"; git log --oneline -1
gh pr create --repo saranatour1/site --base main --head article-polish --title "Animate article titles, smaller description, captioned photo" --body-file - <<'EOF'
## What's in it

- **Title animation:** clicking an article in `/articles` changes the route without a full page reload, and the title and description glide up into their place on the article page. Going back reverses it. It uses Astro's built-in view transitions (`transition:name`), so no extra JavaScript ships.
- **Smaller description:** the line under the article title is now 18px (16px on phones), down from 22px.
- **Centered, captioned photos:** article images are centered in the column. Wrapping one in `<figure>` with a `<figcaption>` adds a centered caption under it. The first article's photo uses this, and `docs/publishing-articles.md` shows how.

This branch is off `main` and is separate from the dependency update in #85.

## Test plan

- [x] In the dev preview, clicking the article in the list routes client-side, and the title and description carry matching transition names on both pages.
- [x] The description renders at 18px; the photo is centered with its caption under it.
- [x] `pnpm build` passes and the built page contains the `<figure>` and caption.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

Animate article titles into place, center captioned photos

- Clicking an article in the list animates its title and description up
  into the article page (matching transition:name on both pages).
- The article description is smaller: 18px, 16px on phones.
- Article images are centered; a <figure> with <figcaption> gives them a
  centered caption. The first article's photo uses it, and the publishing
  guide shows the pattern.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git push -q -u origin article-polish 2>&1 | grep -v "^remote:\|entire"; git log --oneline -1
gh pr create --repo saranatour1/site --base main --head article-polish --title "Animate article titles, smaller description, captioned photo" --body-file - <<'EOF'
## What's in it

- **Title animation:** clicking an article in `/articles` changes the route without a full page reload, and the title and description glide up into their place on the article page. Going back reverses it. It uses Astro's built-in view transitions (`transition:name`), so no extra JavaScript ships.
- **Smaller description:** the line under the article title is now 18px (16px on phones), down from 22px.
- **Centered, captioned photos:** article images are centered in the column. Wrapping one in `<figure>` with a `<figcaption>` adds a centered caption under it. The first article's photo uses this, and `docs/publishing-articles.md` shows how.

This branch is off `main` and is separate from the dependency update in #85.

## Test plan

- [x] In the dev preview, clicking the article in the list routes client-side, and the title and description carry matching transition names on both pages.
- [x] The description renders at 18px; the photo is centered with its caption under it.
- [x] `pnpm build` passes and the built page contains the `<figure>` and caption.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

Both PRs are squash-merged into `main`:
- [saranatour1/site#85](https://github.com/saranatour1/site/pull/85) (dependencies, TypeScript 7.1, Databuddy ID) landed as `74fc562`.
- [saranatour1/site#86](https://github.com/saranatour1/site/pull/86) (title animation, smaller description, captioned photo) landed as `f45b197`.

Your local checkout is now on the updated `main` with its packages installed, and it builds cleanly. I haven't checked whether Cloudflare's production deploy of the merge has finished yet. The previous merge to `main` deployed successfully, and the full build passed on Cloudflare for #85.

Before merging, I checked why Cloudflare was failing on #85. The build passed there, including the new TypeScript 7.1 check. Only the PR preview step failed, so it didn't block the merge.

I got one thing wrong earlier: removing the Databuddy setting didn't fix the PR preview failures. Wrangler now asks for a `previews` block even when it's empty, as `"previews": {}` in `wrangler.jsonc`. That affects only the preview copies Cloudflare makes for each PR.

input.command:
git add wrangler.jsonc && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Add an empty previews block so PR preview deploys run

wrangler preview refuses to run without a previews block, even an empty
one. Previews use the same settings as production.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git push -q -u origin wrangler-previews 2>&1 | grep -v "^remote:\|entire"
gh pr create --repo saranatour1/site --base main --head wrangler-previews --title "Add empty previews block so PR preview deploys run" --body-file - <<'EOF'
Cloudflare's PR checks have been failing at the deploy step: `npx wrangler preview` refuses to run without a `previews` block in `wrangler.jsonc`, even an empty one. The site build itself passes.

This adds `"previews": {}`, so previews use the same settings as production. There are no vars or bindings to override now that the Databuddy ID lives in code (#85).

## Test plan

- [x] `wrangler deploy --dry-run` accepts the config.
- [ ] The "Workers Builds: site" check passes on this PR, which runs `wrangler preview`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

A local Wrangler dry run accepts the new config. The real proof is the "Workers Builds: site" check on #87, which runs the same `wrangler preview` command that kept failing. That check hasn't reported yet, so the fix isn't confirmed. If it passes, the PR is ready to merge.
